scenario.title: Klisura Pass
intro.text:
KLISURA PASS - 6 JAN 1941

Trebeshine Heights, Albania

After your victory at Korytsa we could penetrate deep into Albanian territory. However, we need the strategic important Klisura pass to consolidate our position. You will be the right one for this job. Occupy the Klisura Pass and the surrounding heights of Trebeshine mountain range!

GOAL Take all Allies VH!

NOTE The unit occupying the Klisura Pass, gets the chance of a Leader!
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-1-0-briliant.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.reaction-1-0-briliant.text: Korytsa fell before the Italian command could organise a second line. The advance has become a national triumph, which means the next order will assume triumph is repeatable.
line.reaction-1-1-victory-tactical.text: Korytsa is ours, though the road behind it is crowded with damaged vehicles and newly assigned guards. The city raised morale; it did not shorten the mountains.
line.callback-0.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.callback-0.text: You reached Korytsa before my road reports did. Headquarters has remembered the speed and quietly forgotten how exposed the lead battalion was.
line.callback-1.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.callback-1.text: The quartermaster keeps invoking your Korytsa roads whenever operations gives him an impossible timetable. I dislike admitting that he has a point.
line.callback-2.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.callback-2.text: The Pindus riders are still together. Every headquarters borrows them and none remembers to return them.
line.callback-3.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.callback-3.text: The Pindus screen was dissolved, but its route tables travelled farther than the horses would have.
line.scene-0.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.scene-0.text: The snow has covered the stakes the engineers planted yesterday. A lieutenant just led his platoon in a circle and came back furious with the mountain.
line.scene-1.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.scene-1.text: He can be furious after he finds Ballaban. The Italian reserves use the pass; their food and wounded use the villages. We cannot cut both with the guns we have.
line.decision.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.decision.text: Put the batteries on Klisura and break the lock, or split the columns through Ballaban and Suke. I need one plan before the weather closes again.
line.decision.choice.break-the-pass.text: Concentrate the artillery and break Klisura Pass first.
line.decision.choice.break-the-pass.hint: Spend 50 prestige, give artillery 15 experience, and fully rearm the core.
line.decision.choice.open-the-side-roads: Take Ballaban and Suke while light columns turn the pass.
Give infantry and reconnaissance 10 experience and fully refuel and rearm the core.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-a-0.text: The village columns will hear every shell going somewhere else. Give them extra mortars, or call them screens and spare them heroic instructions.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.choice-a-1.text: They are screens. Klisura receives the guns until the pass opens. Once it does, the villages lose their road and their reason to hold.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.choice-b-0.text: Two columns in this snow will lose contact. I want fixed reporting hours and a flare code even the replacement officers have seen.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.choice-b-1.text: Issue it. Ballaban and Suke fall together; then both columns turn above the pass. No race for the first flag.
